That matters because per-segment structures are FIXED SIZE: each indexed field's null-index allocates two 1 MiB flags_a.dat mmaps (has_values + is_null), byte-verified, so 8 fields x 23 segments = 385.9 MB of padding against 214.3 MB of real index data — 64% of the whole 600.2 MB payload index, >99% empty at 24k points/segment. Also added the resource limits and flush budget the container never had: mem_limit 4g / memswap_limit 6g (2g cushion, and the two must move together or docker grants swap == memory) and stop_grace_period 60s (there was none, so docker's 10s default applied — the SIGKILL-mid-flush condition that cost Lycos ~1,085 points on 2026-08-01). DELIBERATELY did NOT add QDRANT__STORAGE__LOW_MEMORY_MODE, which is the right lever on DeepCast/Lycos and the wrong one here: no_resident loads quantization as if always_ram=false and this collection pins the int8 copy on purpose, so it would have silently undone the 2026-07-30 design. Guard asserts the DERIVATION (64_000 * dim/256), not the literal, so it fails if the embedding dimension moves and the constant is carried over; mutation-verified RED at 64_000. Container is stopped, nothing applied; max_segment_size reaches an existing collection only via ensureStorageLayout() or setIndexingThreshold().]
